bib.title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory

question: How can an LLM agent keep coherent long-term memory across multi-session conversations without passing the full history through its context window?
hypothesis: Extracting, consolidating and retrieving compact salient memories (optionally as a graph) beats RAG and other memory systems on accuracy and approaches full-context accuracy at far lower latency and token cost.
contributions: Mem0: an extraction and update pipeline (ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP chosen by an LLM tool call) over a vector store
Mem0g: a graph-memory variant storing entity-relation triplets in Neo4j
Evaluation on LOCOMO against six baseline categories, with accuracy, token and latency metrics

method.summary: Mem0 processes each message pair with a conversation summary and the last m messages to extract candidate facts with an LLM, then compares each fact with the top s similar stored memories and lets the LLM choose ADD, UPDATE, DELETE or NOOP. Mem0g stores entities and relation triplets in a Neo4j graph, with LLM conflict resolution that marks relations invalid rather than deleting them. Both are evaluated on LOCOMO with GPT-4o-mini.

datasets.name: LOCOMO
datasets.size: 10 conversations, about 600 dialogues and 26000 tokens each on average, about 200 questions per conversation on average
datasets.split: all four non-adversarial categories (single-hop, multi-hop, temporal, open-domain); adversarial category excluded
datasets.preprocessing: Adversarial category dropped because ground-truth answers were unavailable

other.use: inference engine for all Mem0/Mem0g LLM operations (extraction, update, graph extraction, answer generation)
embedding model for RAG and LangMem baselines; Mem0's own embedder is described only as 'dense embeddings'

other.note: paper says 'a separate, more capable LLM'; model not named

inference.samples: J evaluated in 10 independent runs over the entire dataset, mean +/- 1 std reported
inference.prompting: Answer-generation prompt gives memories for both speakers with timestamps, step-by-step approach, answers under 5-6 words (Appendix A); Mem0g prompt adds graph relations for each speaker
inference.retrieval: Mem0: top s=10 similar memories in update phase; m=10 previous messages as context. RAG baseline: chunk sizes 128 to 8192 tokens, k in {1,2}. Mem0g: entity-centric subgraph plus semantic triplet matching above a relevance threshold

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: lexical token-overlap F1 between generated and gold answer

metrics.name: BLEU-1 (B1)
metrics.definition: unigram BLEU against the gold answer

metrics.name: LLM-as-a-Judge (J)
metrics.definition: judge LLM labels answer CORRECT or WRONG given question, gold answer and generated answer; prompt adapted from Packer et al. 2023

metrics.name: Token consumption
metrics.definition: tokens retrieved as context per query (cl100k_base)

metrics.name: Search latency
metrics.definition: time to search memory or chunks, p50 and p95

metrics.name: Total latency
metrics.definition: retrieval plus answer generation time, p50 and p95

eval.protocol: 10 runs for J; baselines LoCoMo, ReadAgent, MemoryBank, MemGPT and A-Mem take published numbers where gpt-4o-mini was the evaluator; A-Mem re-run (A-Mem*) at temperature 0 to get J. OpenAI memory: whole conversation ingested into one chat session, and all generated memories supplied as context (not retrieval of relevant ones).

prompts.text: Your task is to label an answer to a question as "CORRECT" or "WRONG". ... you should be generous with your grading - as long as it touches on the same topic as the gold answer, it should be counted as CORRECT. ... Just return the label CORRECT or WRONG in a json format with the key as "label".

You are an intelligent memory assistant tasked with retrieving accurate information from conversation memories. ... 8. The answer should be less than 5-6 words. ... Memories for user {speaker_1_user_id}: {speaker_1_memories} ... Question: {question} Answer:

Can you please extract relevant information from this conversation and create memory entries for each user mentioned? Please store these memories in your knowledge base in addition to the timestamp provided for future reference and personalized interactions.

evidence.quote: we configured the system with ‘m’ = 10 previous messages for contextual reference and ‘s’ = 10 similar memories for comparative analysis

results.claim: Full-context beats Mem0 and Mem0g on overall J but at about 17 s p95 total latency.
results.setup: LOCOMO, GPT-4o-mini, full 26031-token conversation per query, mean of 10 runs
results.table: Table 2, row Full-context, column Overall J (72.90 ± 0.19%); Mem0 66.88 ± 0.15%

results.claim: Mem0 overall J, and Mem0g overall J.
results.setup: LOCOMO, GPT-4o-mini, k=10 style memory retrieval, 1764 memory tokens; Mem0g is 68.44 with 3616 memory tokens
results.table: Table 2, row Mem0, column Overall J (66.88 ± 0.15%); row Mem0g 68.44 ± 0.17%

results.claim: Mem0 total p95 latency is far below full-context.
results.quote: lower p95 latencies of around 1.44 seconds (a 92% reduction) and 2.6 seconds (a 85% reduction)
results.note: Abstract and conclusion say 91% lower p95 latency; Section 4.3 says 92% for Mem0 and 85% for Mem0g

results.claim: Mem0 has the lowest search latency of all methods.
results.setup: LOCOMO; p95 is 0.200 s; Mem0g search p50 0.476 s
results.quote: Our proposed Mem0 approach achieves the lowest search latency among all methods (p50: 0.148s, p95: 0.200s)

results.claim: Mem0 has relative 26% J gain over OpenAI's memory.
results.setup: LOCOMO, GPT-4o-mini; OpenAI memory given all generated memories as context
results.quote: Mem0 achieves 26% relative improvements in the LLM-as-a-Judge metric over OpenAI
results.note: Overall J in Table 2 is 66.88 vs 52.90, about 26% relative

results.claim: Best RAG configuration peaks near 61% J, below Mem0.
results.setup: LOCOMO, RAG k=2, chunk 256 tokens (k=2 chunk 8192 gives 60.53)
results.table: Table 2, row RAG k=2 chunk 256, column Overall J (60.97 ± 0.20%)

results.claim: Zep scores highest on open-domain questions, above Mem0 and Mem0g.
results.quote: Zep’s J score of 76.60 surpasses Mem0g’s 75.71 by just 0.89 percentage points

results.claim: Mem0g is best on temporal questions; Mem0 is best on single-hop and multi-hop.
results.setup: LOCOMO temporal; Mem0 55.51; single-hop Mem0 67.13 vs Mem0g 65.71; multi-hop Mem0 51.15 vs Mem0g 47.19
results.table: Table 1, row Mem0g, column Temporal J (58.13 ± 0.44)

results.claim: OpenAI memory scores very low on temporal questions because generated memories mostly lack timestamps.
results.setup: LOCOMO temporal; ChatGPT memory with gpt-4o-mini, prompted to include timestamps
results.table: Table 1, row OpenAI, column Temporal J (21.71 ± 0.20)

results.claim: Memory footprint: Mem0 about 7k tokens per conversation, Mem0g about 14k, Zep over 600k.
results.setup: LOCOMO average per conversation; raw conversation is about 26k tokens
results.quote: Mem0 encodes complete dialogue turns in a natural language representation and therefore occupies only 7k tokens per conversation on an average.

results.claim: Zep memories were not reliably searchable immediately; results improved after several hours.
results.setup: Zep platform version on LOCOMO; anecdotal, no timings given. Mem0 graph construction said to finish in under a minute even in worst cases.

results.claim: Mem0 search latency at p95 for LangMem is almost 60 s.
results.setup: LOCOMO; LangMem Hot Path, overall J 58.10%
results.quote: LangMem exhibits even higher search latencies (p50: 17.99s, p95: 59.82s)

limits: Single benchmark (LOCOMO, 10 conversations of about 26k tokens), GPT-4o-mini only; adversarial category excluded.
Full-context still achieves the highest J (about 73%) and the authors present memory as a cost trade-off, not an accuracy win.
Judge model is not named; thresholds t and the triplet relevance cutoff are not given.
OpenAI baseline is given all generated memories rather than retrieved ones, and its extraction cost is excluded from latency; Zep runs used the platform version and a delay of hours affected results.
Graph variant does not help multi-hop (J 47.19 vs 51.15) or single-hop, and adds latency; authors list graph-operation optimisation as future work.
Authors are the Mem0 company team; baseline latency numbers depend on their infrastructure ('infra improvements').
The claim that memory systems keep consistent performance regardless of conversation length is asserted, not measured on longer conversations.

terms.definition: memories stored as directed labeled graph G = (V, E, L) of entities, relations and type labels
ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, NOOP, chosen by the LLM through a function-calling interface
